$comment: Inherited from the backend, where `security-check` was commented out of
pull-request.yaml, so this config had never actually gated anything.
MDRS-15 wires it into CI (.github/workflows/ci.yaml, `security` job).
package-manager was 'npm' and is now 'pnpm': the merged repo has a single
pnpm-lock.yaml and no package-lock.json anywhere, so the npm reader found
nothing to audit.
skip-dev was `true` (inherited) and is now `false`. With it on, `pnpm audit`
reported `devDependencies: 0` — all 1155 of them unaudited — so a new
critical in jest, nx, biome, drizzle-kit or testcontainers would have passed
the gate silently. That directly contradicted the property this file claims
to provide, so the cheaper fix (weaken the claim) was rejected in favour of
auditing dev dependencies too. Cost: 38 high instead of 28, across 31
advisories instead of 24.
The allowlist is a ratchet, not an amnesty. `audit-ci` on c59d467 reports
38 high / 27 moderate / 2 low / 0 critical over 1833 total dependencies.
Entries 1-24 are runtime debt MDRS-8 already routed to MDRS-21 — mostly
transitive next/postcss/sharp, plus @opentelemetry, @nestjs/swagger>js-yaml,
exceljs>brace-expansion, and xlsx (MDRS-8 FU-5: unfloorable, must be
replaced rather than overridden). Entries 25-31 are the dev-only ones the
old skip-dev hid: nx>brace-expansion, @commitlint and jest reaching js-yaml
through cosmiconfig/istanbul, and friends.
Gating on any of them today would red-light every PR. With them listed, the
gate still fails on any NEW high or critical advisory in either dependency
type — which is the property that was missing. low/moderate stay ungated,
as inherited.
When MDRS-21 fixes one, delete its line here in the same PR.
